jobs.title: Leader Amélioration de la Donnée / Data Improvement Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description

Leader Amélioration des Données / Data Improvement Lead

English job description follows***

Description De L'emploi

Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans l'analyse de données et la gestion de la performance, vous avez travaillé sur l'amélioration de processus et la digitalisation, et vous souhaitez évoluer tout en développant de nouvelles compétences ? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Leader en amélioration des données pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance Management basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous collaborez étroitement avec les analystes de performance, les équipes des Opérations et l'équipe de digitalisation.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Performance Management chargée de développer la standardisation et l'amélioration de la qualité des données de performance pour la chaîne de valeur A220, tout en soutenant la feuille de route de digitalisation. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale et l'autonomie, dans un esprit de soutien mutuel et d'apprentissage collectif.

Dans ce rôle, vous agirez en tant que point de contact central et facilitateur entre les analystes de la performance opérationnelle et l'équipe de digitalisation. Votre mission sera d'optimiser l'efficacité des processus d'assemblage de l'A220 en coordonnant l'amélioration des données provenant de divers flux : approvisionnement secondaire, SDO ( Supplier Disruption Over Cost ), coûts récurrents (RC) et CVAT ( Customer Value Added Time ). Vous identifierez les besoins en automatisation, harmoniserez les méthodes d'analyse et assurerez la transition des analyses manuelles vers des solutions digitales robustes pour améliorer la rentabilité globale.

Votre Environnement De Travail

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce Que Nous Prenons Soin De Vous

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride (selon les besoins opérationnels), une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais, service médical sur site, accès à un service de navette publique entre Laval (station de métro Montmorency) et Mirabel, et une application de covoiturage.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos Défis

Assurer le lien principal entre les analystes (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) et l'équipe de digitalisation pour traduire les besoins métiers en solutions automatisées;
Garantir la qualité, la cohérence et l'exactitude des données de performance issues des flux d'approvisionnement et de production;
Harmoniser la définition et le suivi des indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) à travers les différents flux pour assurer une vision transverse de la performance;
Identifier les opportunités d'automatisation des rapports de performance (hebdomadaires, mensuels, trimestriels) et superviser leur mise en œuvre par l'équipe technique;
Consolider les points de blocage majeurs identifiés par les analystes du pôle Performance Management afin de prioriser la feuille de route de digitalisation selon l'impact sur la performance des opérations;
Préparer et présenter des feuilles de route claires et des visualisations de données aux parties prenantes pour soutenir la planification stratégique;
Collaborer avec les départements Opérations, Finances et Qualité pour optimiser la performance globale de la chaîne de valeur.

Votre Profil

Vous détenez un baccalauréat en ingénierie;
Vous détenez un minimum de 10 ans d’expérience dans un système industriel;
Vous possédez une expérience pertinente en analyse de données, en gestion de la performance ou en amélioration de processus;
Vous maîtrisez les outils d'analyse et de visualisation de données tels que Power BI, Skywise et Python;
Vous avez une connaissance approfondie des entrepôts de données, de l'analytique en nuage et de l'automatisation des processus;
Vous possédez de solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et une capacité démontrée à collaborer avec des équipes interfonctionnelles;
Vous avez la capacité de vulgariser des concepts de données complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux équipes opérationnelles et de direction;
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la définition de cadres de mesure de performance et la création de structures d'analyse complexes.

Ce poste peut impliquer des déplacements professionnels.

Déplacements Requis

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant !

Job Description

You have proven experience in data analysis and performance management? Have you worked on process improvement and digitalization, and are you looking to grow and develop new skills? This role is for you!

The A220 Commercial Aircraft Program is seeking a Data Improvement Leader to join our Performance Management team based in Mirabel (Quebec, Canada), where you will collaborate closely with performance analysts, Operations teams, and the digitalization team.

You will be part of the Performance Management team responsible for developing standardization and improving performance data quality for the A220 value chain, supporting the digitalization roadmap. The team is structured to promote cross-functional collaboration and autonomy, fostering mutual support and collective learning.

In this role, you will act as a central point of contact and facilitator between operational performance analysts and the digitalization team. Your mission will be to optimize the efficiency of the A220 assembly processes by coordinating data improvement across various streams: secondary supply, SDO (Supplier Disruption Over Cost), Recurring Costs (RC), and CVAT (Customer Value Added Time). You will identify automation needs, harmonize analytical methods, and ensure the transition from manual analysis to robust digital solutions to improve overall profitability.

Your Working Environment

The A220 commercial aircraft Programme is headquartered in Mirabel, in the greater Montreal area, where the vibrant city of Montreal is just a stone’s throw away. Known for its peaceful and safe environment, the region offers a high quality of life for younger or experienced professionals and families, perfectly balancing career opportunities and outdoor activities that makes it a truly special place to call home.

How We Care For You

Financial rewards: Attractive salary, annual bonus, group insurance plan, pension plan and share purchase plan.
Work / Life Balance: A hybrid working policy (based on operational needs), on-site cafeterias and a highly competitive holiday policy.
Wellbeing/Health: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Discount Program, on-site Medical Service, access to a public shuttle service between Laval (Montmorency metro station) and Mirabel, and a carpooling application.
Individual development: Great upskilling opportunities and development prospects with unlimited access to +10.000 e-learning courses to develop your employability, certifications, accelerated development programmes, national and international mobility.

Your Challenges

Act as the primary liaison between analysts (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) and the digitalization team to translate business needs into automated solutions;
Ensure the quality, consistency, and accuracy of performance data collected from supply and production flows;
Harmonize the definition and monitoring of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across various flows to guarantee a cross-functional view of performance;
Identify automation opportunities for performance reporting (weekly, monthly, quarterly) and oversee their implementation by the technical team;
Consolidate major roadblocks identified by the Performance Management analysts to prioritize the digitalization roadmap based on its impact on Operational Performance;
Strategic Communication: Prepare and present clear roadmaps and data visualizations to stakeholders to support strategic planning;
Collaborate with Operations, Finance, and Quality teams to optimize the overall value chain performance.

Your Boarding Pass

You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering;
You have a minimum of 10 years of experience in an industrial system;
You possess relevant experience in data analysis, performance management, or process improvement ;
You are proficient in data analysis and visualization tools such as Power BI, Skywise, and Python;
You have in-depth knowledge of data warehousing, cloud analytics, and process automation;
You possess strong problem-solving skills and a demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams;
You have the ability to simplify complex data concepts for operational and executive leadership teams;
You have proven experience in defining performance measurement frameworks and creating complex analytical structures.

Business Travel May Be Required For This Position.

Travel requirements: < 5% (Occasional trips to the United States)

jobs.title: Director, Data Centres and New Large Loads - Power Market
jobs.description:
Type of position:
Regular

An Overview Of Your Future Role At BBA

BBA supports all players across the energy ecosystem, including power generation, transmission and distribution. We also support large industrial energy users, mainly in the mining, oil and gas sectors. More recently, we’ve seen growing demand from a new category of large energy consumers, particularly data centres. To date, BBA’s involvement in the data centre market has been largely reactive, with developers and builders reaching out to us for our expertise in grid interconnections and power systems. Going forward, BBA will take a deliberate and proactive approach to this market by establishing a dedicated data centre business line.

Drawing On More Than 45 Years Of Experience Solving Complex Electrical Challenges, BBA’s Go-to-market Strategy Will Be Guided By The Following Principles

Avoid commodity building design and leverage strategic partnerships where appropriate
Focus on projects larger than 25 MW
Lead the high-voltage scope
Lead grid integration activities
Lead substation design and delivery
Lead generation strategy development

An Overview Of Your Mandates And Responsibilities

You'll source and ensure successful delivery of power projects to meet the energy needs of large-load clients, primarily data centres. You’ll also occasionally support other industrial, community and utility clients operating in remote or partially grid‑connected environments. Initially, the role will focus on regional clients across Canada and gradually expand to include the U.S. market.

As a renewable power professional, you’ll lead the modelling, optimization and delivery of complex energy projects involving renewable technologies, including wind, solar PV, BESS, thermal and hydroelectric power. Your work will include studies, roadmaps and project execution.

BBA operates within a matrix structure, and the New Large Loads business line you’ll lead has both national and international focus. The business line is accountable for defining market strategy and overseeing sector performance. To deliver on its mandates, it works closely with BBA’s operational teams and disciplines across Canada and the USA. While most projects are executed through these regional teams, the business line may also directly manage and deliver certain strategic initiatives.

Business development

Coordinate the development and execution of BBA’s data centre market strategy
Build and maintain strong relationships with key clients and stakeholders across the data centre, utilities and industrial sectors
Support the development of short‑, medium‑ and long‑term opportunity pipelines while identifying cross‑selling opportunities for BBA’s services
Support project sourcing efforts by identifying opportunities that align with regional priorities across Canada and evolving data centre power needs
Contribute to proposal development, client positioning and pursuit strategies for power and energy mandates
Maintain a strong understanding of energy market trends, particularly for data centres, off‑grid, hybrid and utility‑linked power systems

Operations

Serve as project manager and technical lead for selected strategic projects, including project development support, feasibility studies, roadmaps and execution mandates
Provide subject‑matter expertise in the modelling, optimization and integration of renewable and hybrid power systems (wind, solar PV, CSP, BESS, thermal storage, hydroelectric)
Oversee technical reviews and coordinate engineering and design activities across disciplines
Work closely with BBA’s multidisciplinary teams across Canada to ensure execution excellence and alignment with client objectives
Help develop internal expertise in data centre development, power system optimization, hybrid energy solutions and renewable integration
Support the development of tools, methodologies and reference models for studies, roadmaps and system optimization
Participate in knowledge sharing and thought leadership activities, including internal training, technical contributions and industry engagements

Do your qualities and values match our corporate culture?

Business acumen
Strategic vision
Action and results-driven
Ability to see beyond established standards
Constantly seeking sustainable and agile solutions
Rigour and ethical
Accountability and entrepreneurship
Client-oriented with existing network
Organizational agility

An ov
erview of BBA’s total rewards

Annual premium program for regular employees
Onsite mobility premium
Time bank
Cellphone fee reimbursements
Group insurance plan from the first day of employment, including disability insurance and a telemedicine program
Retirement savings plan
Annual vacation and sick leave
Premium for employee referrals

BBA considers many factors when determining the annual base salary, including location, market, education, relevant and demonstrated work experience, technical assessment, qualifications, certifications and other relevant skills.

Summary Of Certifications And Job Requirements

Engineering degree in a related discipline from a recognized university
At least 15 years of relevant experience
Experience in data centre development and execution, wind and/or solar power energy, consulting engineering, business development and project execution
Registered as a Professional Engineer in Canada
Experience in equipment selection, capital cost and operating cost estimates
Available to travel to domestic or international destinations is required

About BBA

BBA is one of Canada’s leading private consulting engineering firms, with over 45 years of experience serving the energy and natural resources industry.

Our people are the foundation of our success. Their passion and excellence have earned us recognition as one of Canada’s Best Employers and Best Managed Companies , and we’re committed to fostering a workplace where everyone feels empowered to grow, lead and be themselves.

Our teams bring together engineering, environmental and commissioning expertise to deliver practical, innovative and sustainable solutions—from strategy to execution. With 20 offices across Canada, the U.S. and Latin America, we combine local presence with international reach, offering clients close collaboration and field-ready support.

Learn more about our culture and projects on LinkedIn or connect with our talent team.

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.
Proven success leading strategic sourcing initiatives, complex commercial negotiations, and major procurement programs.
Deep understanding of engineering governance, capital project delivery, EPC contracting models, procurement practices, and commissioning processes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and contract administration.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Construction Engineering, or a related technical discipline; P.Eng. designation strongly preferred.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and travel as required to support projects across Canada.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration
jobs.description:
Lead financial and corporate stewardship for Curve Lake First Nation

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $150,000 to $180,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build the systems, teams, and financial stability that will support the Nation for the next decade

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions. These are financial governance, human resources, policy and planning, communications, and information technology. Finance sits at the heart of the role. You will be accountable for sound financial oversight, audit readiness, and strong relationships with funders, auditors, and the First Nations Financial Management Board.

Where We Are Now

The Nation is strengthening its administrative foundations; you will provide interim oversight and stabilization across Finance, HR, IT, and Policy and Planning while building out your team. You will also lead the selection and implementation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

A key priority is moving the Nation from year-by-year funding to Indigenous Services Canada’s 10-year grant. This means completing the Financial Management Board certification process and putting the controls and reporting in place to qualify. Predictable, long-term funding will give the Nation far greater confidence in its forecasting and planning.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean a fully staffed division with your managers in place, trusted relationships with Chief and Council, staff, and community, strengthened audit readiness and internal controls, and the ERP selection well underway.

By the end of year two, you will have led the Nation through FMB certification and embedded consistent financial, governance, and administrative practices. You will also have put systems in place that keep reporting and audits on schedule, giving the organization a solid foundation for the years ahead.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Leading multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and annual operating and capital budgets
Serving as executive lead for external audits, including selecting the appropriate audit firm and working closely with auditors throughout the process
Ensuring compliance with funding agreements, Indigenous Services Canada reporting requirements, and the Nation’s Financial Administration Law
Leading the Nation through the FMB certification and 10-year grant process
Structuring and staffing the finance function so reporting deadlines are consistently met, working with bookkeepers, analysts, and account managers
Providing executive oversight of HR, IT, policy and planning, and communications through four direct-report managers
Overseeing the selection and implementation of an ERP system, along with cybersecurity, data governance, and digital modernization
Providing financial analysis, risk advice, and recommendations to the Executive Director and Chief and Council

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Finance and Administration document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a post-secondary degree or diploma in finance, accounting, or a related financial field
, along with at least 5 years of senior-level experience in financial administration or corporate services,
including experience working within a First Nation organization.

The following are required:
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation
Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM) or Certified Aboriginal Professional Administrator (CAPA) designation
A master’s degree in public administration, finance, or a related field
Direct experience with the First Nations Financial Management Board, FMB certification, or the 10-year grant process
Strong working knowledge of audit processes, GAAP, and funder reporting requirements
Experience working with Indigenous Services Canada and other funding agencies
Experience overseeing multiple functional areas such as Finance, HR, IT, and Planning

As our ideal candidate, you are a disciplined, systems-minded leader who keeps deadlines met and audits clean, and who knows how to build a finance team organized around its reporting obligations. Your understanding of First Nation finances runs from day-to-day funding agreements through to the path toward long-term grant funding. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

In exchange for your hard work and dedication, you will receive a highly competitive salary of $150,000 to $180,000
negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance
Comprehensive Benefits Plan: extended health care, dental, vision, life and long-term disability, etc.
Competitive Pension Plan with up to 7.5% employer matching
40 paid hours for Special/Personal Leave Bereavement Leave
Paid time off for 17 designated days, including National Indigenous Day, Christmas Day, etc.
Generous vacation accrual
Paid sick days
Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Take on a senior leadership role that builds lasting financial stability and strong systems for the Curve Lake First Nation community. Apply now!

jobs.description:
Req Id:
431516

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell’s AI Fabric initiative is pioneering a secure, sovereign AI compute network across Canada. This transformative portfolio includes seven large-scale, high-density data centres, anchored by a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2GW flagship site in Regina, Saskatchewan.

As Program Director, you will be accountable for the end-to-end delivery of the national data centre build program—orchestrating scope, schedule, budget, and cross-functional execution across multiple concurrent sites. You'll be the integrating force connecting construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls into one predictable, well-governed program, ensuring Bell delivers these mission-critical facilities on time, on budget, and to standard as the initiative scales aggressively nationally.

Key Responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery accountability for the national data centre build program, integrating scope, schedule, budget, and quality across multiple concurrent sites.
Orchestrate cross-functional execution across construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls, ensuring alignment to program objectives.
Establish and govern the program delivery framework—stage gates, milestones, governance cadence, and decision rights—across the portfolio.
Own the integrated master schedule and program-level budget, driving predictability, transparency, and schedule discipline across all builds.
Lead program-level risk management, change governance, and interdependency management, escalating and resolving systemic issues before they impact delivery.
Provide executive-level program reporting to AI Fabric and Capital Programs leadership, translating complex delivery status into clear, decision-ready insight.
Manage program financials, forecasting, and capital planning in partnership with finance and program controls.
Drive resource planning and prioritization across sites, balancing competing demands as the program scales
Build and mature Bell's program delivery capability at a formative stage, embedding repeatable processes, playbooks, and lessons learned across the fleet.
Serve as a senior point of escalation and executive interface for site directors, functional leads, and external delivery partners.

Critical Qualifications

15+ years leading large-scale capital program delivery, with direct experience on hyperscale or mission-critical data centres (multi-site / multi-billion-dollar portfolios preferred)

jobs.description:
FNHA Overview

The First Nations Health Authority is a diverse and transformational health organization of professional, innovative, and dedicated team members and leaders.

The first of its kind in Canada, FNHA works as a health-and-wellness partner with BC First Nations to support self-determination and decision-making to improve health outcomes.

The First Nations Health Authority is committed to respecting diversity within our workforce; preference will be given to individuals who identify as First Nations, Inuit, or Métis. All interested First Nations, Inuit or Métis individuals are encouraged to apply. The First Nations Health Authority has a mandate to increase First Nations, Inuit or Métis representation in the workforce. Applicant skills, perspectives and lived experience may be matched for this role, or other opportunities within the FNHA.

FNHA is proud to have been named one of BC’s Top Employers for 2026. Learn more about why we were selected here .

Title:
Chief Financial Officer and Vice President of Information Management and Information Technology

Salary:
$226,000- $282,000 per year (targeted salary)

Contract
: Permanent

Hours:
Full-time, 37.5 hours per week (core hours 9am-3pm Mon-Fri)

Location
: Metro Vancouver– Hybrid (Hybrid working is an option in line with FNHA’s flex work policy). Please note, this role will be relocating to our new office building in North Vancouver on Tsleil-Waututh Nation (TWN) land, south of Mount Seymour Parkway in Spring 2027.

About The Role

The Chief Financial Officer and Vice President of Information Management and Information Technology (CFO) - reporting to the CEO - holds an executive role that shapes and directs the financial and digital strategy in alignment with the FNHA's objectives for First Nations health in British Columbia. Entrusted with overseeing all financial and fiscal management aspects of a highly complex, multi-partner organization, the CFO handles a range of functions, from budgeting and financial reporting to forecasting and risk management, ensuring these elements support the organization's mission and quality services. Additionally, the CFO provides strategic direction in leading Information Management and Information Technology, critical functions that ensure the organization's data, digital health, and information security infrastructure to ensure service excellence.

Tasked with articulating and achieving the vision of the financial and technology systems for the organization, the CFO is at the forefront of driving change management, streamlining financial and technology operations, and fortifying the organization's financial and information infrastructure. Collaborating closely with internal teams, First Nations communities, and external partners, including government bodies, the CFO ensures that funding allocation and utilization are strategically aligned with FNHA's mission. Additionally, the role includes strategically leading and mentoring a diverse team, guiding their professional development, inspiring a commitment to excellence, and maintaining accountability in all financial and technology practices.

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of financial and technology expertise, leadership skills, cultural safety and humility, and a dedication to the FNHA's values and seven directives, contributing to the organization's vision of enhancing healthcare for First Nations people across the province. With a solid track record in finance and technology leadership, including contract and procurement management, the selected individual will be versed in developing funding and IT strategies that meet the unique healthcare needs of First Nations communities.

new_jobs.description:

432862

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.
Proven success leading strategic sourcing initiatives, complex commercial negotiations, and major procurement programs.
Deep understanding of engineering governance, capital project delivery, EPC contracting models, procurement practices, and commissioning processes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and contract administration.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Construction Engineering, or a related technical discipline; P.Eng. designation strongly preferred.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and travel as required to support projects across Canada.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.
